name: mound

attributes.attribute: a place of belief built long ago by the Megalithic people
a barrow said to hold the city of the fair folk
risky to pass at night or at Beltane and Samhain
the fair folk of the mounds, in old tale the Tuatha De Danann

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A mound, often called a fairy mound, is a place of folk belief across the Celtic world. The land holds traces of a people far older than the Celts. This unknown folk of the Megalithic Civilization lived about 5000 B.C.E. and raised many works of stone. Stonehenge and Bru na Boinne are famous, but simple passage graves and dolmens are far more common. The Celts took these old works as holy and told of fairies who dwelt inside. A small natural hill or a drumlin could also be seen as a mound. Old barrows were said to hold small cities where the fair folk danced. It was risky to pass a mound at night or at Beltane or Samhain. The hidden door might open and lead a walker into an endless dance. The Irish call these homes the sídhe. The folk within are the daoine sídhe, the people of the mounds.

key_results: Record the mound as a folk place of the Megalithic people.
